transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex (AE), Priya (SE) - Redwood; Jordan (Eng Mgr), Maya (PM), Samir (SRE) - Midcity Payments
Links referenced: pricing deck (link shared in chat), benchmark spreadsheet (google.com/spreadsheets/example), security pack (drive/redwood-security.pdf)

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining; I'm Alex, I'm the AE on the account, and priya here is our solutions engineer who will walk through the Optimize recommendations. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jordan: good, thanks. quick heads up - we've got about 45 minutes, happy to dive deep on the cost model.
[00:15] Priya (SE): awesome, i'll share my screen, but if the auto-transcript picks up weird words sorry in advance, sometimes it says 'kay vee' for KV.
[00:22] Maya: no worries, go ahead.

--- Intro / Context gathering ---
[00:28] Priya: quick context check - Jordan, you mentioned earlier you're evaluating hosted vs dedicated for our inference. can you confirm current traffic? avg requests per day, typical session length?
[00:36] Jordan: yeah, so current pilot traffic is about 1 million API calls/day, mostly chat-style sessions. avg request size is ~180 user tokens, system prompt is ~120 tokens, and we see about 3 prior turns on average. latency SLO is 200ms p95 for critical flows, and cost is obviously a big concern.
[00:52] Alex: and do you have any KV/prefix cache today?
[00:56] Samir: no, we don't. we tried some internal caching but it's brittle with context switching.

[01:05] Priya: ok great — goal for today: show how Redwood Optimize recommends batching + prefix/KV cache settings, walk through a cost model example with your numbers, and propose a lightweight pilot to measure real benefits.

--- Technical walkthrough: prefix/KV cache ---
[01:20] Priya: so two pieces: prefix (or prompt) caching and KV cache. prefix cache stores the left-context --- system prompt and recurring history snippets that are identical across sessions. KV cache is more at the model level: we cache key/value pairs from the transformer layers for repeated prefixes so we avoid re-computing previous tokens when a user resumes a session.
[01:43] Jordan: is that the same as what we call "hot prompt caching"?
[01:46] Priya: yeah similar, different layers. in practice prefix cache can cut prompt tokens that hit from the model by typically 20-50% depending on reuse. KV cache can be even more impactful for long conversations because it prevents re-generation of attended state — effectively reduces per-response compute.
[02:05] Maya: how do you handle staleness? like if system prompt changes, do we invalidate?
[02:08] Priya: good q. we version prefixes and have TTL and explicit invalidation hooks. your rollout could start with a conservative TTL (e.g., 24h) and then adjust.

--- Batching ---
[02:18] Priya: batching is the other leaver. Redwood supports adaptive batching that groups concurrent requests to better utilize GPU throughput while respecting latency SLOs. fixed batching is simpler but can add tail latency. we commonly recommend adaptive with a max batch size tuned to your model and target p95.
[02:36] Alex: worth noting, batching reduces tokens-per-second cost by increasing GPU utilization; however, if you push for very low p95 latency (e.g., <100ms), you might choose smaller max batch sizes which lowers the cost benefit.

--- Cost model example (numbers) ---
[02:52] Priya: i built a sample cost model using the numbers you gave: 1M calls/day, avg 180 user tokens, 120 system tokens. so naive without caching you'd generate ~300 tokens per request on average.
[03:05] Priya: baseline compute: 1M * 300 = 300M tokens/day. with our hosted pricing examples, roughly that's X GPU-hours — in our sheet i've translated to $/day but i'll paste the row: baseline cost ~$6,800/day (this is illustrative, exact depends on model/quantization).
[03:25] Jordan: that seems high, can you show how caching helps?
[03:28] Priya: sure — assume prefix cache hit rate of 45% (midpoint for chat with recurring templates) and KV cache effective reduction of 30% on remaining generations, combined with adaptive batching that gives 20% utilization improvement. the combined effect reduces token generation by about 60% in this scenario.
[03:50] Priya: so 300M * 0.4 = 120M tokens/day -> cost down to ~$2,700/day. that's a ~60% cost reduction in the model and serving layer. again these numbers depend on hit-rate and your session patterns.
[04:06] Samir: what's the assumption on prompt length if users attach receipts or long docs?
[04:10] Priya: good point. for long attachments we recommend offloading to embeddings + retrieval and only include concise context in the model prompt. our Optimize recommendations flag long-turn sessions and propose retrieval pipelines to reduce token payloads.

--- Tradeoffs and objections ---
[04:28] Jordan: our SLO is pretty tight on p95. if adaptive batching adds 30ms median but 100ms tail sometimes, how do we guarantee SLO?
[04:37] Priya: we tune batching thresholds and use fastpath routing for critical routes: requests marked 'low-latency' go to smaller batch size or dedicated lanes (can be in Dedicated capacity or hosted with reserved burst). we can also set per-route SLO targets in the Console.
[04:52] Maya: what's the engineering effort? we have limited infra time.
[04:55] Alex: that's the thing — Optimize recommendations are prescriptive and the pilot can be turnkey: Redwood runs a benchmark with your sample traffic, we provide config suggestions and a small infra template for KV/prefix cache integration; dev time for initial integration is often 1-2 sprints depending on team bandwidth.

--- Security & deployment ---
[05:12] Maya: SOC2 questions - we need audit logs, KMS for keys, and VPC peering for private deployment.
[05:18] Alex: we have the security pack; Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC with audit logs. we'll share SOC2 + ISO docs.
[05:24] Samir: do we need dedicated capacity to get guaranteed p95?
[05:27] Priya: dedicated helps for predictability; we can start on hosted with reserved capacity and then move to Dedicated if you need strict isolation and SLAs. both can use the same Optimize tooling and config.

--- Live example: bench spreadsheet walk-through ---
[05:40] Priya: i'll walk through the sheet: here is the baseline row, then i added rows for cache hit-rate scenarios: conservative (20% prefix hit), realistic (45%), optimistic (70%). also separate cols for batching uplift and kv effectiveness.
[06:02] Priya: show numbers: baseline tokens/day 300M; conservative -> 240M; realistic -> 120M; optimistic -> 60M. cost scales roughly linear with tokens for same model variant.
[06:16] Jordan: can you attach model variants? like quantized 8-bit vs fp16?
[06:19] Priya: yes — sheet includes model variant multiplier: 8-bit quant gives about 35-45% cost cut vs fp16, accuracy delta evaluated in our model catalog. we'll recommend a validation set to confirm quality.

--- Implementation pattern ---
[06:35] Priya: recommended pilot path: 1) collect sample traffic + target routes, 2) Redwood runs a 48-72 hour benchmark in staging using your traffic footprint, 3) measure real prefix hit rates and batching latency profiles, 4) produce tuned config (batch sizes, TTLs, route-level fastpath) and projected K-cost/cost-savings.
[06:55] Maya: what's the expected time to results?
[06:58] Priya: about 2-3 weeks end-to-end for the initial pilot: 1 week integration + 48-72h run + analysis.

--- Questions and clarifications ---
[07:08] Jordan: are there any GDPR-data residency issues with caching? does Redwood persist prefixes?
[07:12] Alex: prefixes can be stored encrypted and we support regional storage; you can also opt for ephemeral KV stores or customer-managed keys to control residency. we'll include that in the security pack.
[07:21] Samir: curious on eviction policy — do you support LRU or LFU?
[07:24] Priya: yes we support LRU, TTL-based and custom policies; for your use case we usually do LRU with a TTL window aligned to session activity.

--- Recap & next steps ---
[07:35] Alex: quick recap: Redwood Optimize can likely cut your serving cost by ~40-60% in a realistic scenario using prefix + KV cache + adaptive batching, but we need a pilot to measure actual hit rates. next steps: Alex sends pricing + bench sheet by 5/14; Priya drafts pilot plan by 5/18; Jordan to share sample traffic and SLOs by 5/19.
[07:58] Jordan: sounds good. also can you include a rough T-shirt estimate for engineering effort?
[08:02] Alex: yep, i'll include a 1-2 sprint estimate and a engineers-hours breakout in the email.
[08:07] Maya: and please share the security pack and SOC2 artifacts.
[08:10] Alex: will do.

[08:15] Priya: any other technical deep-dive we should follow up on? we can do an SE-only call to test playback of your traffic and tune batch sizes.
[08:22] Jordan: let's do that after we review the pilot plan.

[08:28] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll send the follow-ups.
[08:31] Maya: thanks all.

End of transcript.
